boneless-beef-chuck.name: Beef for Braising
levels: 203 °F collagen fully rendered, shreds with a fork
boneless-beef-chuck.note: A braise is not cooked to safe, it is cooked to tender. Chuck and stew meat need hours above 190 °F before they stop being tough.

boneless-chicken.name: Chicken Breast
levels: 150 °F pasteurized after roughly 3 minutes held, still juicy
boneless-chicken.note: Pasteurization is time at temperature, not a single number. Breast held at 150 °F for 3 minutes is as safe as breast that touched 165 °F, and it is noticeably less dry.

boneless-chicken-thighs.name: Chicken Thigh
boneless-chicken-thighs.note: Dark meat is full of collagen that only breaks down well past done, so a thigh pulled at 165 °F is safe but chewy.

cod-fillets.name: White Fish
cod-fillets.note: Cod, tilapia, and halibut have no fat to hide overcooking, so the window between flaking and chalky is only a few degrees.

flank-steak.name: Steak
flank-steak.note: Skirt and flank are thin enough that carryover overshoots easily, so pull them 5 °F under the target.

ground-turkey.name: Ground Turkey
ground-turkey.note: Grinding spreads surface bacteria through the meat, so ground poultry has no range below the minimum.

pork-shoulder.name: Pork Shoulder
pork-shoulder.note: Like beef chuck, shoulder is a collagen cut and the safe minimum is nowhere near done.

raw-jumbo-shrimp.name: Shrimp
raw-jumbo-shrimp.note: Shrimp go from tender to rubbery in under a minute. The shape is a better cue than the thermometer: a C is done, an O is overcooked.

salmon.name: Salmon
